No - at your mountain town's elevation water boils below 212F, so 45 minutes in an open pot will leave dried kidney beans undercooked and hard. Expect roughly 50-100 percent longer cooking time (often 2-3 hours) and test for tenderness rather than trusting the package clock; a pressure cooker is the far easier fix. Also note the safety point that applies at any elevation: soak the beans, discard the water, and make sure they get a full rolling boil for at least 10 minutes to destroy the toxin in raw kidney beans.
